headline: Profit rises on higher coal prices despite output decline
summary_short: China Coal Energy's H1 2026 net profit attributable to shareholders rose 5.8% y/y to CNY 8.14bn (IFRS +11.8% to CNY 8.19bn) despite an 8% y/y drop in commercial coal production to 61.95Mt, as self-produced coal ASP rose 11.5% to CNY 524/t.
summary_long: Revenue held at CNY73.13bn while commercial coal production fell 8% y/y to 61.95Mt as safety inspections tightened following the May Xinji mine incident; management does not expect the crackdown to ease this year. Self-produced coal ASP rose 11.5% to CNY524/t on richer product mix (more high-calorific, waterproof coal), while unit cost rose 8.6% to CNY285.69/t on lower-output fixed-cost absorption and outsourced-to-self-operated team conversion. Net profit attributable rose 5.8% CAS / 11.8% IFRS to CNY8.14bn / CNY8.19bn. Operating cash flow rose 28.6% to CNY9.86bn. Interim dividend CNY0.184/share declared. H2: management aims to recover lost output and hold the original production plan; Phase 2 Yulin polyolefin (900kt/yr) starts up November 2026.
confidence_notes: The primary interim report PDF (en.chinacoalenergy.com) could not be machine-parsed after two fetch attempts (binary PDF, not HTML/text). Filing-depth figures and management quotes below are corroborated via a transcript of China Coal Energy's own H1 2026 results briefing (board secretary Jiang Qun, CFO Chai speaking directly to the filed interim report's numbers) rather than the PDF text itself -- same underlying primary content, not analyst commentary. Revenue is described by the company as 'held at CNY73.13bn' with no precise prior-year comparator quoted, so its y/y delta is marked '~flat' rather than a computed percentage. EPS (Q2, wire-derived, CNY0.35) is Yahoo's quarter-only split from earningsChart and is NOT directly comparable to the company's own H1-cumulative EPS (CNY0.61 CAS / CNY0.62 IFRS) -- China Coal Energy reports on a semi-annual (H1/H2) cadence, not discrete calendar quarters -- kept as separate KPI rows to avoid conflating the two series. Commercial coal sales (119.7Mt) had no year-ago comparator quoted in the source, so delta_basis is 'none'.

drivers.explanation: Safety inspections tightened sector-wide after the May Xinji mine incident; management said the crackdown "will not ease up this year," cutting output 8% y/y.
Management attributed pricing gains to a better product mix -- more high-calorific and waterproof coal -- with average thermal coal calorific value up nearly 200 kcal/kg.
Higher fixed costs from lower output, plus higher labor costs from converting outsourced mining teams to self-operated status, drove unit cost up 8.6% y/y.
Higher self-produced coal selling prices added CNY3.3bn to profit and the chemicals segment added CNY878m, partly offset by CNY1.17bn lost to lower self-produced sales volume.

Management called H1 results resilient despite a difficult operating environment, citing price and product-mix gains plus a chemicals-segment profit contribution offsetting the safety-driven output decline.
